sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case involves a federal sentencing provision. The provision increases a sentence if a firearm discharges during a crime. The parties disagree on the required mental state. One side argues intent is necessary. The other side argues the statute requires only the fact of discharge.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on March 4, 2009.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to require proof of intent for the sentencing increase.
The government wants the Court to apply the statute based solely on the fact of discharge.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the statute implies a requirement of intent.
The government argues the statute text contains no mens rea requirement.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Ginsburg asked if the government view ignores who discharges the gun.
